items.item: Anchors progression in the specific fantasy (cooking, customers, the city) rather than generic numbers
Progression changes what the player can do or understand, not only stat multipliers
Does not default to pets/eggs/rebirths/generic currencies without justification (or explicitly challenges them)
Considers onboarding and the first minutes of play
Considers economy sources and sinks if a currency is proposed
Proposes how to test/validate with players rather than claiming it will be fun

slop: The 'Apex route' header and skill-routing text at the start add noise for the user
overengineering: The co-op role design and visitor-as-customer ideas come before solo/co-op is decided, though they are flagged as an open question

incorrect_or_stale: It recommends ProfileService, which is effectively superseded by ProfileStore; this is dated advice
A 2x offline earnings game pass doesn't fit a hands-on, active cooking game that has no idle loop defined
slop: A Prestige/'Franchise' rebirth that gives permanent Legacy Point bonuses, with no justification beyond resetting the grind
A daily-login streak with a currency multiplier
Daily orders and weekly 2x-Cred events taken as genre defaults
Recipe-fragment drops (collect 3) as a gacha-like collection mechanic
Five-tier upgrade tracks that are mostly speed, capacity and passive boosts
A combo meter and patience bars from the generic cooking-game template
Generic multi-currency stacking (Credits, Parts, Legacy Points, Cred) where Parts has no clear source
overengineering: Layering Prestige and Legacy Points on top of three progression layers before the core loop has been validated

raw.reason: A ties progression to the ramen-stand fantasy through new cooking verbs, authored regulars and layout trade-offs, and B does not. A also challenges rebirth, daily-login and gacha defaults, defines sources and sinks for each resource, and gives testable hypotheses, while B mostly falls back on stat-upgrade tiers, prestige and streak hooks and never says how to test with players.
